title: creative courage in the digital void
content:
the tender work of releasing your work into the void

sharing space camp
 

this is a 30 second animation I created for my new class, sharing space camp — serving both as a trailer/preview of the course, and an animated syllabus of what we’ll cover together, in a cyclical 4 week journey.

originally this trailer had text and a voice over, but I decided that the visuals wanted to tell their own story. I also wrote a post about the process of how I made this.

everything about sharing your work is a practice — something you do (something I did, and am still doing) even when it feels very hard, meaningless, or futile.

  • holding the tenderness of what you made — in the palm of your hands

  • not abandoning yourself to the pressure of platforms

  • the practice of releasing your work into the void

  • being with the silence, loneliness, and emptiness

  • allowing your work to feel generative & sustainable

  • creating new worlds with your creativity

  • creating your own containers & capsules for sharing

  • inviting others to discover it, slowly

  • journeying onwards, and repeat

the trick is that you keep doing this, until it feels easy.


*

the origin text I didn’t include

I wrote more here about how I started with this text — then evolved beyond it.

the thing is, you are already in outer space.
it’s just more comforting to believe
that you need to be acknowledged in order to exist.

the platforms lure us with “community.”
promising safety from the abyss.
institutions anoint us with legitimacy

but really, in the cosmic internet wild,
there are no rules.
you don’t need permission.
it was never about them.
it was only ever about you —

all that matters is your courage
your relationship to the tender,
whispering things inside
letting them go —
is letting them live.

the work is simple, not easy —
speak into the void
until it feels as effortless
as breathing.

you are a cosmic traveler,
this is how you conjure new worlds.
it must be you.
